title: Mirror-MLA canonical latent cache
hypothesis: A single rank-4 MLA latent cache plus a shared rank-2 basis of per-view K/V up-projections and small coefficients can retain synthetic attention output quality across aligned and mildly heterogeneous views at <=75% of full independent projection-plus-cache bytes; private low-rank residuals will identify where additional per-view state becomes necessary.
physical_object: one shared rank-4 content latent sequence C
mirror_coordinate: per-view coefficients over two shared K/V up-projection basis maps, optionally with private residual rank q
logical_multiplicity: 8 logical K/V projection roles read from one latent cache
controls: hard-tied MLA with one K/V up-projection

development.selection_metric: per-view attention output NRMSE, actual serialized deployment bytes, and projection/decode MAC proxy over frozen rho/rank grid

success_gate: For rho=0 and rho=0.1, at least one q<=2 point across all audit seeds has output NRMSE <=0.02, complete payload <=75% of independent, and incremental projection/decode MAC <=2x independent. Mirror-specific attribution additionally requires beating native shared-basis/PCA on function, bytes, or compute.
failure_gate: No q<=2 point meets the joint error/bytes/compute gate for rho=0.1, or no tested regime beats the independent payload while retaining error <=0.02. Exact alias to native shared-basis control is FAIL for Mirror-specific value regardless of generic compression feasibility.
boundaries: Synthetic FP32 attention operator screen only; no trained MLA model, language NLL, GPU kernel, or production throughput claim.
Basis and coefficients are fit from the same synthetic operator bank for controlled capacity measurement; no learning-efficiency or natural task claim.
All fresh seeds and ranks were locked before any measurements; no audit tuning.
